takeaways.t: **President Vladimir Putin agreed on 12 Nov to let European representatives join the next round of Ukraine peace talks, US envoy Steve Witkoff said after their Kremlin meeting;** the same day President Zelensky said new restrictions were affecting the US-made satellite communications Ukraine uses at the front. [7, 8]

**Iran's Revolutionary Guard said on 13 Nov it had targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for an attack on a telecom tower in Sirik,** the first Iranian claim of an attack on US military assets in a Gulf country since early September, Reuters reported; Washington and Manama had not commented. [9]

**The Pentagon has “greenlit” a permanent US troop presence in Poland, with the White House to decide in early December,** Defense News reported on 12 Nov; Defence Minister Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz called it “our absolute priority”. [10]

**The Tweede Kamer passed the 2027 tax plan on 12 Nov with 76 of 150 seats and without the VVD,** after a Pro and Volt amendment that taxes wealth more; Prime Minister Rob Jetten meets deputy prime ministers Dilan Yeşilgöz (VVD) and Van den Brink (CDA) this morning to hold the coalition together. [5]

**Finland's Defence Forces said on 12 Nov they had detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area the day before,** and that Finland faces no immediate military threat; Estonian media reported a small navy ship returned to St Petersburg. [11, 12]

**The Bundestag passed the Bundeswehr infrastructure acceleration law on 12 Nov with CDU/CSU and SPD votes,** granting the forces exceptions from environmental and nature-protection law for building and expanding military sites. [13]

pick.t: If you read one thing: Bertelsmann's transatlantic trust survey. 72% of Americans call Europe a trustworthy partner and 36% of Europeans say the same of the United States, yet 61% of Europeans still want the US military presence kept or increased; Germans (25%) and the French (30%) trust Washington least, Romanians, Poles and Lithuanians most. items.h: Putin agrees to let Europeans join the next round of Ukraine talks
items.body: Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met President Vladimir Putin in the Kremlin on 12 Nov, a day after the Abu Dhabi round ended. [7] Witkoff told Russian state television: “The Europeans will join at the next meeting, which we consider to be a very important moment because they are our partners and it's important to us that they take part.” [7] Putin said Washington must work with its European allies to understand whether they want peace or war in Ukraine. [7] Witkoff told CNN at Vnukovo airport: “We've restarted it. We've set a new meeting.” [8] Zelensky said new restrictions were affecting the US-made satellite communications Kyiv uses on the battlefield and called the US approach of discussing a new European security order with Russia “a bit strange”. [7]
items.next: Witkoff and Kushner were due to brief Zelensky in Dublin; no date or venue for the next round is published, and Europe has not named its representative. [8, 15]

items.h: Drones and missiles hit Kyiv and Kramatorsk on 12 Nov; five killed
items.body: The Ukrainian Air Force counted 123 long-range attack drones, 72 of them jet-powered, plus Iskander-M, S-400 and Zircon missiles overnight into 12 Nov; by about 08:00, 89 drones and five S8000 Banderol munitions were downed, with drone impacts at 17 locations. [16] Mayor Vitali Klitschko said one person was killed and eight injured in Kyiv in the overnight and daytime strikes. [16] Between 06:30 and 19:00 on 12 Nov the Air Force counted 143 drones and S8000 Banderol/Dan-T missiles, of which 124 drones and two missiles were downed. [17] Four people were killed and six injured in Kramatorsk the same day. [18] Ukraine's General Staff claimed 2,150 Russian personnel and 1,013 drones for the day. [19]
items.next: The Air Force count for the night into 13 Nov was not out by 05:30 CET. [18]

items.h: Finland detects a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland
items.body: Finland's Defence Forces said on 12 Nov that they had detected “a strike” on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area a day earlier. [11] A spokesperson wrote to Reuters: “The Finnish Defence Forces detected… a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland area and has monitored the development of the situation,” and said Finland is not under any immediate military threat. [11] Estonian media reported that the vessel was a small Russian navy ship that later returned to St Petersburg; Finnish broadcaster Yle cited Ukraine's Security Service as saying it carried out the attack. [11, 12] Smoke rose over the Ust-Luga port area after a drone attack on 11 Nov, in a Reuters photograph. [12]
items.next: The Finnish Defence Forces declined further detail; Russia had not commented by 05:30. [11]

items.h: Revolutionary Guard says it targeted a US radar in Bahrain
items.body: Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps said on 13 Nov it had targeted a US early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for what it called an air attack on a telecommunications tower in Sirik, Hormozgan province, which state agency IRNA said was hit by “enemy fire” on 12 Nov. [9] Its statement, carried by Tasnim, said: “Should these violations and acts of aggression recur, the IRGC Aerospace Force stands in full readiness to engage without limits.” [9] The IRGC-affiliated Fars agency said the radar was “targeted and destroyed”; Washington and Manama had not commented, and Reuters called it the first Iranian claim of an attack on US military assets in a Gulf country since early September. [9] Bahrain hosts the headquarters of the US Navy's Fifth Fleet. [9] Al Jazeera's live page reported that President Trump said Gulf partners had asked him to pause further strikes on Iran. [20]
items.next: No date is published for US–Iran talks on the Qatar track; Israel's security cabinet order of 11 Nov to prepare for a possible attack stands. [21]

items.h: Hoaxes and Ukraine dominate the European Political Community in Dublin
items.body: Leaders from more than 40 European countries met in Dublin on 12 Nov for the European Political Community summit. [15] Taoiseach Micheál Martin said those behind the recent attacks seek to “create confusion, sow division and weaken public confidence in our democratic systems” and added: “We will not allow them to succeed.” [15] More than 3,700 Italian schools received hoax bomb warnings on 12 Nov, a day after 6,300 schools got similar alerts. [15] Zelensky told the summit that Russia's negotiators in Abu Dhabi had no mandate to discuss a ceasefire and that Ukraine's Black Sea de-escalation proposal got a negative answer. [22] UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced that the UK was the first country to sanction all 10 of Russia's major oil producers and chaired a side meeting on defence support for Ukraine. [23]
items.next: The EU–UK summit follows next week; nominations for an EU envoy for the talks are expected in December. [23, 24]

feature.title: Week on the board, 7–13 Nov: talks restart, Iran claims a hit in Bahrain, 74 entries across 13 theatres
body: Talks set the pace on the Russia–Ukraine board. The trilateral round ran on 10–11 Nov in Abu Dhabi and ended with agreement on a large-scale prisoner exchange and no other breakthrough. [25] Witkoff and Kushner met Putin on 12 Nov; Witkoff said a new meeting was set and that Europeans would join it. [8, 7] Strikes continued alongside: two Russian cruise missiles crossed Moldovan airspace on 11 Nov, and Finland detected a strike on a Russian warship in the Gulf of Finland the same day. [26, 11]

The Gulf board moved from mines to a direct claim. The Revolutionary Guard said two tankers hit mines near the Strait of Hormuz on 7 Nov. [27] Israeli media reported on 11 Nov that the security cabinet had ordered preparations for a possible attack on Iran. [21] On 13 Nov the IRGC said it had targeted a US radar in Bahrain. [9] In Israel, President Herzog gave Gadi Eisenkot the mandate to form a government, and Hezbollah's Naim Qassem ruled out a state monopoly on the group's weapons. [28, 29]

Elsewhere the week was steadier. Taiwan's defence ministry counted 11 PLA aircraft sorties on 7 Nov and four on 11 Nov, and Kim Yo-jong rejected the UN Secretary-General's call to restore inter-Korean channels on 10 Nov. [30, 31, 32] In the north, two Chinese heavy-lift carriers that crossed the Arctic route were held near Andøya, and ten Joint Expeditionary Force navies signed a Northern Navies Initiative aboard HMS Prince of Wales on 12 Nov. [33, 34] The World Food Programme put DR Congo's acutely food-insecure population at 28.8 million. [35]

The Black Sea board closes the week on a date: Gagauzia votes for its governor and People's Assembly on 15 Nov. [36] The Balkans carried court news only, with the UN court refusing Jovica Stanišić early release and a Bosnian court sentencing three men for 1992 abuses in Bosanski Novi. [37, 38]

leads.title: Belgium's interior and foreign ministers split in public over naming Iran for the fridge attacks
leads.teaser: Bernard Quintin points to Iran in the Chamber; Maxime Prévot says it is too early, as France has already named an IRGC unit.
rows: Interior Minister Bernard Quintin told the Chamber on 12 Nov that there are serious indications Iran is behind the early-November cyberattacks on supermarket refrigeration in Belgium, and asked Foreign Affairs to back France's call for EU sanctions. [46, 47] Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot said it was “trop précoce” (“too early”) to confirm and that attribution is his department's call. [46]
The Belgian Chamber, 12 Nov; the Belgian incidents date from early November, and France attributed its October attack to an IRGC unit on 9 Nov. [46]
Not attributed by Belgium; the federal prosecutor is investigating, and Iran's embassy in Brussels denies involvement. [46]
Prévot said Belgium already backed EU sanctions on Iranian actors over cyberattacks on other states; no decision to summon the Iranian ambassador. [46]
The federal prosecutor's findings, and whether Belgium joins France's sanctions request. [46]
leads.sw: Baseline requirement 4 (food and water): a host nation that cannot agree who attacked its food cold chain will be slower to ask NATO for help with the next one, and Belgium hosts SHAPE.

pattern: **Attribution gap:** Belgium's interior and foreign ministers disagreed in public on 12 Nov over naming Iran for the fridge attacks; France named an IRGC unit on 9 Nov. [46]
**Hoaxes:** 6,300 Italian schools on 11 Nov and 3,700 on 12 Nov received hoax bomb warnings, and the Taoiseach opened the Dublin summit on the theme. [15]
**Sanctions:** the UK sanctioned all 10 of Russia's major oil producers on 12 Nov. [23]

**Espionage:** Nvidia's chief executive Jensen Huang resigned on 11 Nov after an affair with an executive whom US intelligence reports had identified as working for China's Ministry of State Security, The Verge reported. [48]
**Cyber:** NCSC-NL published 11 advisories on 12 Nov covering Ivanti, Fortinet, Citrix, SAP, Barracuda, Node.js and Apache products. [49]

week.t: Eleven incidents were logged for 7–13 Nov, against 17 the week before: three influence operations (the fabricated Merz quote on the Nord Stream trial, disinformation after the Kraków shooting and the Italian school bomb hoaxes), three airspace or hoax cases (aerostats and two Banderol missiles over Moldova, hoax threats in Ireland), two drone cases (air alerts in Latvia and an object from Belarus over Lithuania), one cyber case (the NoName057(16) list naming Italy's foreign minister), one sabotage (signal cables at Köln Messe/Deutz) and one espionage arrest (a US soldier of the Allied Rapid Reaction Corps near Gloucester). [15] On the response side, France named an IRGC unit for the October fridge attack on 9 Nov, the US charged three men over the Fairford plot on 10 Nov, Belgium's ministers split on naming Iran on 12 Nov and the UK sanctioned Russia's ten largest oil producers. [46, 23]

hybrid.note: One new incident, the Italian school hoaxes; the morning's hybrid news is mostly about attribution and response.

europe.h: UK sanctions all 10 of Russia's major oil producers
europe.body: UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham announced at the European Political Community in Dublin on 12 Nov that the UK had become the first country to sanction all 10 of Russia's major oil producers, EUobserver reported. [23] He also chaired a side meeting on defence support for Ukraine. [23] EU foreign policy chief Kaja Kallas said in Dublin she would “very much like the United Kingdom to return to Europe”, ahead of next week's EU–UK summit. [23]
europe.sw: Sanctions on Russian oil output bear on the energy revenue behind Russia's 2027 defence budget, the force NATO's eastern-flank plans are sized against.

europe.h: Belgian ministers clash over Iran as De Wever defends the budget
europe.body: Interior Minister Bernard Quintin said in the Chamber on 12 Nov that serious indications point to Iran behind the early-November fridge cyberattacks, and Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot answered that it was “trop précoce” (“too early”) to say so. [46, 47] Quintin told VRT there were “voldoende elementen” (“sufficient elements”) for his remarks. [47] The same day Prime Minister Bart De Wever faced repeated criticism in the Chamber over the federal budget, RTBF reported. [51] The King hears De Wever's report on 16 Nov.
europe.sw: Belgium hosts SHAPE, so a stalled federal budget reaches the host-nation-support funding and civil-preparedness commitments Allied Command Operations relies on.
europe.fy: Nothing to do; Belgian supermarkets are trading normally.

countries.h: 444 reads Merz's letter as pressure on Hungary over EU budget money
countries.body: 444 reported on 12 Nov that Chancellor Friedrich Merz used Prime Minister Péter Magyar's Berlin visit on 10 Nov to tell Ukraine-sceptic member states that there is “nincs ingyen ebéd” (“no free lunch”): they cannot stay out of the shared Ukraine financing and still draw on the common budget. [52] The paper reads this as a veiled threat to hold up other money questions in the EU budget for 2028 to 2034 unless every state joins. [52] It is the paper's reading of Merz's letter, not a Commission or Hungarian government statement, and the article is partly paywalled. [52] Magyar said on 10 Nov that borrowing to fund Kyiv is not acceptable for Hungary.
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 2 (energy) and 1 (continuity of government): Hungary's resilience spending leans on EU money, so linking it to Ukraine financing ties Budapest's civil preparedness to its Ukraine stance.

q.t: Nem lehet kimaradni a közös pénzügyi kötelezettségvállalásból, majd lehívni a forrásokat a közös költségvetésből, mintha mi sem történt volna.
q.en: You cannot stay out of the shared financial commitment and then draw funds from the common budget as if nothing had happened.

countries.h: Anti-corruption foundation asks parliament to examine Kaliňák over arms-dealer links
countries.body: The foundation Zastavme korupciu (Let's Stop Corruption) asked the National Council's committee on incompatibility of functions on 12 Nov to examine Defence Minister Robert Kaliňák over his links to the Czech arms dealer Michal Strnad, TASR reported. [53] It says Kaliňák's firm Kallan Consulting was paid by a Strnad company for services while the ministry was arranging contracts for Strnad's firms, a link that continued after Kaliňák took office. [53] These are the foundation's allegations; no finding has been made. [53]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 1 (continuity of government): Slovak procurement by direct award under security exemptions is the channel for allied ammunition and equipment buys, and a committee case against the minister tests its oversight.

q.t: Takýto postup vytvára vážne podozrenie z klientelizmu a korupcie.
q.en: Such a procedure creates a serious suspicion of clientelism and corruption.

countries.h: Bundestag passes the Bundeswehr infrastructure acceleration law
countries.body: The Bundestag passed the Bundeswehr-Infrastrukturbeschleunigungsgesetz (Bundeswehr infrastructure acceleration law) on 12 Nov; CDU/CSU and SPD voted for it, the Greens and the Left against, and the AfD abstained. [13] The law gives the forces exceptions from environmental and nature-protection law and adjusts the rules on protected military areas and land procurement, so that sites can be used and expanded faster, with a strategic property reserve. [13] The draft puts extra costs for shared accommodation at up to €210 million over five years. [13]
countries.sw: Baseline requirement 7 (civil transportation) and host-nation support: faster building and expansion of German military sites is the reception and staging capacity that reinforcement through Germany depends on.

q.t: Dafür stimmten CDU/CSU und SPD, dagegen Bündnis 90/Die Grünen und Die Linke.
q.en: CDU/CSU and SPD voted for it; Alliance 90/The Greens and The Left voted against.

items.h: Ten JEF navies sign a Northern Navies Initiative aboard HMS Prince of Wales
items.body: The Royal Navy and its Joint Expeditionary Force (JEF) partners signed a Northern Navies Initiative aboard HMS Prince of Wales in Oslo on 12 Nov, during the International Sea Power Conference. [34] It aims to make the JEF NATO's maritime vanguard in the North Atlantic, High North and Baltic, able to act early and pass into NATO command if the Alliance mobilises at scale, and names risks to undersea infrastructure and hybrid aggression. [34] First Sea Lord Gen. Sir Gwyn Jenkins said: “The threats we face are multiplying and that we must rise to the challenge before us.” [34]
items.sw: A JEF force built to hand over to NATO command is the maritime flank of the northern reinforcement picture that a land HQ plans beside.

items.h: Leaked draft NATO guidance would plan for a European war or out-of-area missions, not both
items.body: Index reported on 12 Nov, citing a leaked draft of NATO's Political Guidance, that allies would no longer be asked to field enough forces for a large European war and several smaller missions outside Europe at once, but for one or the other. [54] The paper writes that the draft runs to 2029 and treats a major European contingency as overriding every other priority. [54] NATO has not published the document. [54]
items.sw: Political Guidance sets the capability targets behind NATO's defence planning cycle, which in turn size the forces a JFC's regional plans can count on.

items.h: Germany and Poland hire SATIM to analyse military satellite imagery
items.body: SATIM, a Polish maker of AI-based satellite-imagery analysis, has contracts with the German and Polish militaries, Defense News reported from Warsaw on 12 Nov. [55]
items.sw: Shared commercial imagery analysis between the two largest eastern-flank armies is a data source a land HQ may be asked to fuse.

items.h: Royal Navy orders Saab radars for its K3 Scout counter-drone boats
items.body: The Royal Navy awarded Saab a £15 million contract on 12 Nov for Sea Giraffe 1X radars to fit to Kraken Technology's K3 Scout uncrewed surface vessels, an autonomous “drone seeker” first shown earlier this year. [56] The boats are meant to give persistent surveillance and early warning against aerial threats to ships, ports and critical national infrastructure. [56]
items.sw: Port protection by uncrewed radar pickets is the kind of host-nation capability that reception at North Sea ports would draw on.

items.h: SeaOwl and KNDS unveil the Tracus kamikaze surface drone at Euronaval
items.body: French robotics firm SeaOwl and KNDS announced at Euronaval in Paris on 12 Nov a cooperation agreement to develop and field Tracus, an uncrewed surface vessel with a 30 kg warhead for anti-ship and anti-swarm missions. [57] It began as a training target for the French Navy and launches from a box up to 7 metres above the water. [57]
items.sw: European one-way surface drones copy Ukraine's Black Sea playbook into allied inventories.

items.h: Army plans to buy small attack drones as needed rather than stockpile them
items.body: Army Materiel Command plans to manufacture small attack drones to deliver rather than to store, Breaking Defense reported on 12 Nov. [58] Jon Strzelec of the command said Russia can counter a new drone within 72 hours; about 10,000 of the first 30,000 Drone Dominance drones had reached units for training. [58] The Pentagon plans $1 billion of Drone Dominance spending over two years. [58]
items.sw: Replace-not-repair sustainment changes the logistics annexes a land HQ writes for small-drone units.

items.h: Google puts Gemini 4 Hydrogen into Search's AI Mode
items.body: Google moved Search's AI Mode to its Gemini 4 Hydrogen model on 12 Nov, saying it handles complicated questions better; Google's Robby Stein called it “the biggest model upgrade to Search yet”. [59] Google did not publish benchmark figures with the announcement. [59]
items.sw: Search answers written by a frontier model become a source staff officers cite without seeing it, which raises the bar for source checking in open-source work.

items.h: Study finds chatbots showed risky shopping links in up to 15% of conversations
items.body: A study that tested Gemini, Perplexity and ChatGPT on shopping questions found that in as many as 15% of conversations the chatbots displayed “risky” URLs, including fake retail websites, The Verge reported on 12 Nov. [60]
items.sw: Chatbots that cite fake sites are an influence and fraud channel that hybrid actors can seed.

The Senate agreed to vote on H.Con.Res. 93 no later than 20 Nov. [61]
FY2026 levels and no new starts until then.

words.quote: The permanent presence of US troops in Poland is our absolute priority and we will not abandon this matter.

depth.title: Seven decisions in a week: Poland, special operations, drones and the Iran vote
body: The week's decisions ran from Warsaw to the Senate floor. On 10 Nov Secretary Pete Hegseth met Poland's Władysław Kosiniak-Kamysz at the Pentagon; by 12 Nov Defense News reported that the Pentagon had “greenlit” a permanent US presence in Poland, leaving the final call to the White House in early December. [10] The same day the Senate agreed to vote on H.Con.Res. 93, the House resolution directing the removal of US forces from hostilities with Iran, no later than 20 Nov. [61]

Inside the department, the largest organisational move concerns special operations. A Hegseth memo dated 2 Nov and released on 12 Nov would raise the assistant secretary for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict to an under secretary of strategic services, a title only Congress can grant; meanwhile the office moves up the order of precedence, gains a seat on the Joint Requirements Oversight Council and in budget reviews, and receives 75 civilians and 25 Joint Staff members within 60 days, with the comptroller told to find $45 million a year. [62] Kori Schake of the American Enterprise Institute said Hegseth lacks the authority to make the change. [62]

Money and kit decisions followed. The department issued three loans totalling $450 million to US space companies on 11 Nov. [63] Army Materiel Command set out a buy-to-deliver model for small attack drones on 12 Nov, citing Russian counters within 72 hours. [58] On Capitol Hill the House passed a bill on 12 Nov that would let combat-injured retirees with under 20 years of service draw full retired pay and VA disability compensation without the dollar-for-dollar offset, and Senator Chris Van Hollen led a push to strip US–Israel industrial-base provisions from both NDAA texts. [64, 65]

What did not move is as telling. No assumption-of-command date has been published for Lt. Gen. Admiral at USAREUR-AF, the Europe posture review's options have not been made public, and the continuing resolution still expires on 11 Dec.

dod.h: Pentagon backs a permanent US troop presence in Poland
dod.body: The Pentagon has “greenlit” the permanent presence of US troops in Poland, with the final decision due from the White House in early December, Defense News reported on 12 Nov, citing Poland's defence ministry. [10] The ministry said Secretary Hegseth told Defence Minister Kosiniak-Kamysz on 10 Nov that “everything is going in a good direction”. [10] Warsaw has offered Bydgoszcz, Poznań, Szczecin and Wrocław as sites for about 5,000 troops.
dod.sw: Bases west of the Vistula sit on the reinforcement routes from the North Sea ports that JFC Brunssum's plans depend on.

dod.h: Hegseth moves to raise the top special operations civilian to service-secretary rank
dod.body: A memo from Secretary Hegseth dated 2 Nov and released on 12 Nov would make the assistant secretary of defense for Special Operations and Low-Intensity Conflict an under secretary of strategic services, which needs Congress. [62] Until then the office moves to Code 2 in the order of precedence and gets a seat on the Joint Requirements Oversight Council and in budget reviews; 75 civilians and 25 Joint Staff members transfer within 60 days and the comptroller must find $45 million a year. [62]
dod.sw: A stronger special operations civilian chief changes who sets priorities for the SOF that NATO's special operations headquarters draws on in Europe.

news.h: Army CID seeks commercial tools to watch the darknet and encrypted apps

research.title: Winning Time: Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces and the New Dimension of War
summary: Honcharuk argues that the decisive contest in the Russia–Ukraine war is the speed of adaptation, which he calls the “Time Domain”: the interval between a new capability reaching the front and the enemy's effective counter. Mass decides how long a side can keep paying, he writes, and speed decides what each payment buys. [67]

He treats Ukraine's Unmanned Systems Forces as the first force built to compete in that domain. Most senior officers opposed a separate branch in late 2023 on the logic of “No domain, no branch of service”, but Ukraine created it anyway; the force holds about 2.5% of Ukraine's personnel and, citing The Wall Street Journal, “has accounted for roughly a third of Russian losses this past year”. [67]

His working model is the “Combat Hub”, which puts operations, analytics, research and production under one command and runs three cycles: daily fixes, iterations of about six weeks and changes of about six months. The evidence comes from the 412th Brigade “Nemesis”: in its first seven months 47 crews flew more than 950 sorties and destroyed more than 520 targets, including over 360 pieces of equipment he values at $308 million, for 107 airframes lost worth about $3.2 million. [67]

He recommends adding a time axis to planning, buying adaptation cycles rather than systems, funding by verified effect, and creating a small insulated unit with its own budget line. Visible adaptation machinery deters, he argues, but “a window that is closing invites” attack. [67]
findings: **Share of force:** about 2.5% of Ukraine's personnel, credited (via the WSJ) with roughly a third of Russian losses in the past year. [67]
**Nemesis output:** 47 crews, 950+ sorties and 520+ targets in seven months, with 360+ pieces of equipment valued at $308 million. [67]
**Cost exchange:** 107 airframes lost, worth about $3.2 million, roughly $100 of Russian equipment per $1 of airframe. [67]
**Range:** the strike copter grew from about 6 kg over 10 km to nearly 100 km reach. [67]
**Fibre optics:** by April 2025 Ukraine had more than 20 certified fibre-optic drone models from 11 producers. [67]
**Procurement:** the drone marketplace is to carry 70% of drone buying in 2026, paid in points for strikes verified in Delta. [67]
research.method: A practitioner's essay, not peer-reviewed. The brigade figures come from the unit's own flight records, which are not public, and the author advised the first commander of the force and co-founded a defence technology firm. It cannot show that the Combat Hub, rather than other factors, produced the results, or that the model transfers to armies without Ukraine's networks. Yesterday's long read pointed to the same essay; it is summarised here because no peer-reviewed military paper could be read in full this morning.
research.sw: For Brunssum: it turns a vague lesson into a planning question a land HQ can test, how many weeks an adversary needs to counter a new system, and argues that training and procurement should be scored on adaptation time as well as inventory.

research.title: Unequal Trust, Shared Interests: European and American Views on the Future of Transatlantic Relations
research.authors: Brandon Bohrn, Courtney Flynn Martino, Daniela Schmidt
summary: The brief compares European and American opinion on the transatlantic partnership, from an August 2026 survey run by Nira Data for the Bertelsmann Stiftung's eupinions project and the Bertelsmann Foundation North America. Its central finding is lopsided trust: 72% of Americans call Europe a trustworthy partner, while 36% of Europeans say the same of the United States. [14]

Both publics still want cooperation: 62% of Europeans and 73% of Americans back deepening the partnership whoever is in the White House, security and defence top both lists, and 61% of Europeans and 66% of Americans want the US military presence in Europe kept or increased as European spending rises. [14] Trust varies sharply by country, from 25% in Germany and 30% in France to 60% in Romania, 58% in Poland and 57% in Lithuania. [14]
findings: **Trust gap:** 72% of Americans trust Europe; 36% of Europeans trust the US and 64% call it untrustworthy, up 10 points since September 2025. [14]
**Ally ranking:** Europeans naming the US as the EU's most valuable ally fell from 51% (2024) to 29% (2026); the UK rose from 13% to 20%. [14]
**US presence:** 61% of Europeans and 66% of Americans want it kept or increased; 16% and 10% want it ended. [14]
**Independence:** 73% of Europeans and 52% of Americans say the EU should go its own way. [14]
**China:** 65% of Europeans and 72% of Americans back cutting economic dependence on China even at short-term cost. [14]

head: Who says the partner is trustworthy
Share

research.method: Online survey by Nira Data in August 2026, weighted to national demographics: EU n = 18,514 and US n = 5,294, ages 18 to 69 only; Lithuania is weighted on fewer variables. It measures stated opinion at one moment and cannot show what governments will do or why trust moved. [68]
research.sw: Support for a US presence is weakest in the two biggest European allies and strongest on the eastern flank, which is where host-nation politics around US forces will diverge.

research.title: AI as Shared Business Infrastructure: Firm Growth and the Distribution of Gains (NBER Working Paper 36003)
research.authors: Panle Jia Barwick, Lu Fang, Jinhan Liu, Huilan Xu, Zhe Yuan
summary: The authors study a leading Chinese e-commerce platform that built generative AI into the software merchants use to run their stores: a content tool from April 2024 and a business-operations tool from July 2024, free for a month and then RMB 99 (about $14) a month. [70]

Matching 148,770 adopting firms with annual sales under RMB 5 million to 77,347 non-adopters in a difference-in-differences design, they find adoption raises monthly sales by 51.6% and orders by 47.0%, with little change in price per order. The gain is largest for the smallest firms, 61.5% in the bottom sales quartile against 10.3% in the top, because producing the same content at market prices would cost the median small firm 22.7% of annual sales against 0.4% for the largest. [70]
findings: **Size gradient:** +61.5% in the bottom quartile, +10.3% in the top. [70]
**New customers:** sales to new customers +75.6%; new products +66.2%. [70]
**Routine work:** listing updates per product +124.8%; staff time per order −5.6%. [70]
**Market effect:** high-friction categories saw more entry and total sales, with little sign of business-stealing from non-adopters. [70]
research.method: Matched-cohort difference-in-differences on platform records from October 2023 to July 2025, with instrumental-variable checks and a category-level spillover test. Adoption was a choice, and the authors say their tests cannot fully rule out selection; it covers small goods sellers on one Chinese platform. [69]
research.sw: It is rare firm-level evidence that AI supplied as shared infrastructure helps the smallest firms most, which bears on how Europe's small businesses gain from AI they do not build.

philosophy.where: Part I, chapter 13, “Of the Naturall Condition of Mankind, as concerning their Felicity, and Misery”
philosophy.tradition: Medieval and early modern (Augustine, Aquinas, Spinoza, Hobbes, Locke)
philosophy.quote: “And from this diffidence of one another, there is no way for any man to secure himselfe, so reasonable, as Anticipation; that is, by force, or wiles, to master the persons of all men he can, so long, till he see no other power great enough to endanger him: And this is no more than his own conservation requireth, and is generally allowed.”
philosophy.translation: Hobbes's English of 1651, original spelling, as in the Project Gutenberg e-text prepared from the Pelican Classics edition (ed. C. B. Macpherson), checked word for word. [71]
philosophy.gloss: Hobbes has just argued that people are roughly equal in strength and hope, so any two who want the same thing become enemies, and he names three causes of quarrel: competition, diffidence (distrust) and glory. [71] This passage draws the consequence of distrust: where no one can read another's intent and no common power exists, striking first is the most reasonable form of self-protection, and he insists it is no more than self-preservation requires. [71] The next sentence adds that a few who enjoy conquest beyond what security needs force even the moderate to expand or perish, which carries the chapter to its “warre of every man against every man”. [71] The strongest objection is Rousseau's in the Discourse on the Origin of Inequality (1755), Part One: Hobbes gives natural man the pride and fear that only society produces, so the war he describes is a social artefact, not a state of nature; game theorists add that his own logic of anticipation can be broken by repeated dealings and reputation, as the Stanford Encyclopedia's entry sets out. [72]
philosophy.why: Which plan or posture on your desk would a partner read as defensive only after a signal you have not yet sent?

deep.title: Lithuania: the highest share of GDP, and the bill that comes with it
body: Lithuania now spends one of the largest shares of its economy on defence of any NATO ally, and carries one of the larger budget deficits to go with it. The government's draft 2027 budget allocates more than €4.8 billion to defence, 5% of projected GDP and about €35 million more than in 2026; the 2026 share was higher, at 5.38%, so the share falls even as the euro figure rises. [73] The State Defence Council agreed in early 2025 to spend 5% to 6% of GDP a year from 2026 to 2030. [73]

The trajectory is steep. NATO's 2025 expenditure report puts Lithuania at 0.88% of GDP in 2014 and an estimated 4.00% in 2025, with military personnel rising from 8,600 to 19,500 and equipment rising from 14.06% of defence spending to an estimated 45.84%, while personnel costs fell to 25.29%. [74] Vilnius is buying capability, not a larger payroll.

The money has three named purposes: air defence, hosting a German brigade and building a national division. [75] The German brigade was inaugurated in May 2025 and is to be fully operational with up to 5,000 troops by 2027. [76] The €710.5 million approved from the State Defence Fund for 2026 shows the split: €504.7 million for the national division, including tracked infantry fighting vehicles, tanks and simulators, €49 million for the German brigade's infrastructure at the Rūdninkai training area and €34.7 million for mines and other obstacles. [77]

The cost shows on the fiscal side. The general government deficit is projected at 3.8% of GDP in 2027, above the 3% Maastricht line, with debt at 48.2%, and the prime minister has tied most spending beyond revenue to the 5% goal and indexed benefits. [73] By early October only 43.92% of this year's defence appropriations had been spent, and the opposition Nemunas Dawn party criticises delayed buys, purchases outside public procurement and advance payments for kit that arrives in a year or two. [75]

The argument for a land headquarters is that Lithuania shows how fast money can be committed and how slowly it turns into delivered capability. The binding limit is no longer the budget line but absorption: contracts, infrastructure and training ground for a German brigade and a national division at the same time. Plans that count Lithuanian or German forces in the Baltic by date should carry that delivery risk, not the appropriation, as the planning factor. [75, 76]

items.h: Tax plan passes with 76 seats as the VVD votes against
items.body: The Tweede Kamer passed the 2027 tax plan late on 12 Nov with the narrowest possible majority, 76 seats, built on the left and without the VVD. [5] The VVD voted against after a Pro and Volt amendment, agreed with D66 and CDA, that raises tax on people with large assets. [5] D66 and CDA won Denk and the Partij voor de Dieren shortly before the vote, the latter with a higher tax on private jets and a promise that a rise in train fares is off the table. [5] VVD parliamentary leader Ruben Brekelmans called the day “ontluisterend” (“dismal”). [5]
items.sw: The VVD's Finance Minister Eelco Heinen must now carry out a plan his party voted against, and the 2027 defence budget passes through the same strained coalition.
